English: Brush Fence
A simple barrier of thorny brush and crude stakes, hastily erected to mark camp boundaries and slow the approach of raiders.
Reed Palisade
A lightweight palisade of bundled reeds and woven matting, offering minimal protection but a clear sign of settlement organization.
Earthwork Rampart
Raised mounds of earth reinforced with turf and timber, forming a defensive ring and a symbol of growing permanence.
Timber Wall
Heavy timber walls bound with rope and iron spikes, providing solid defense and a clear message of territorial control.
Watchtower Gate
A fortified gate flanked by wooden watchtowers, allowing sentries to keep a vigilant eye on the horizon for enemy approach.
Double Palisade
Twin timber palisades with a ditch in between, greatly strengthening the defense and slowing would-be attackers.
Moated Park
A broad ditch filled with water and marsh vegetation encircles the camp, deterring attackers and symbolizing prosperity.
Defended Outwork
Advanced outer defenses including obstacles, traps, and watch posts, making assaults on the camp far more costly.
Fortress Enclosure
A formidable complex of interlinked palisades, earthworks, and towers, forming a near-impregnable seat of steppe power.
Grand Steppe Redoubt
The ultimate nomadic stronghold: vast ramparts, multiple defensive rings, and towering wooden bastions, inspiring awe and unity among all clans.
